passages.original: Quare, vix mortuo Cœlestino, et in rjus sedem Xysto suffecto, hujus fidem ct apostolicum vigorem Julianus tentare ausus cst, cum, ad eUn datis supplicibus libellis, catholicam tidem profiteri simulabat, ut pristinum rp scopatus honorem et munera p ontifox ei rest tueret. Rem narrat Prosper Aquitanus in Chronico, addens præterea Julianum non ab ali» fuisse elusum quam a sancto Leone tunc Romanae Ecclesiæ archi- diacono, qui omnium viriuln suarum contentione apud sanctum pontficem eDit ut a simulata hæretici hominis I pœnitentia sibi atque toti Ecclesiæ caveret.
passages.english: Therefore, scarcely had Celestine died and Xystus been put in his see, when Julian dared to test his faith and apostolic vigour, since, having submitted petitions to him, he pretended to profess the catholic faith, so that the pontiff might restore to him the former honour and offices of the episcopate. Prosper of Aquitaine relates the affair in his Chronicle, adding moreover that Julian was foiled by none other than Saint Leo, then archdeacon of the Roman Church, who with the full exertion of all his powers prevailed upon the holy pontiff to guard himself and the whole Church against the feigned penitence of the heretic.
passages.notes: Several scanning errors corrected (e.g. 'rjus' = ejus, 'rp scopatus' = episcopatus, 'p ontifox ei rest tueret' = pontifex ei restitueret, 'eDit' read as egit).

passages.original: Novissimus autem eorum editor sibi persuadct exeunte anno 428 , vel ineunte anno 429 , scriptas fuisse. Ita ad marginem annotavit pag. 89. Si deiude epistolarum argumen a perpendamus, in iis palam Prosper testatur Pelagianae hæreseos reliquias in Galliis et in plerisque aliis regionibus adauctas fuisse; maximas quoque querelas excitatas adversus ejusdem Augustini opuscula, et praesertim contra doctrinam libro de Correptione et Gratia explicaLam. Quis autem afUrmare velit jam tum Prosperum carmen iliud de Ingratis cum cæteris libellis a Photio laudatis concinnasse cum has epistolas scriberet? Nonne in iis recensuit gravissmas dilficilioresque quaestiones a Pelagianis motas, quas clara luce ab illo sibi aperiri cupiebat, et, quasi in mularum rerum intelligentia nutans, lumen ex novis Augustini scriptis efflagitabat' Galliam pene totam fuisse commotam , cum Prosper h;ec scriberet, priori epi tola declarat, et propterea licri studebat S.
passages.english: Their most recent editor, however, is persuaded that they were written at the end of the year 428 or the beginning of 429. So he noted in the margin on p. 89. If we then weigh the contents of the letters, Prosper openly testifies in them that the remnants of the Pelagian heresy had grown in Gaul and in very many other regions; and also that very great complaints had been raised against the works of that same Augustine, and especially against the doctrine set out in the book On Rebuke and Grace. But who would wish to affirm that Prosper had already composed that poem On the Ungrateful, together with the other booklets praised by Photius, at the time he was writing these letters? Did he not in them review the very grave and more difficult questions raised by the Pelagians, which he desired to have opened to him by [Augustine] in clear light, and, as if wavering in the understanding of many matters, did he not demand light from new writings of Augustine? That almost all Gaul was in commotion when Prosper wrote these things he declares in the first letter, and for that reason he was eager that he might be made more learned by the wisdom and erudition of the holy

passages.original: Præsertim cum ab Augustino, duobus in libris , videlicet de Praedestinatione et de Duno Perseverantiæ, paulo ame diem ejus emortualem conscriptis, objectas sibi a Prospero et llilario Massiliensium ct Pelagianorum Quæstiones enodatas fuisse intelligimus. Quando vero Augustinus obierit, nArrat Possidius in Augustini Vita scribens : Anno 430, quinto kalendas Septembris S. doctorem humanæ vitæ debitum persoliisse , quo tempore Vandali Hipponem tertium jam mensem obsidebant.
passages.english: Especially since we understand that the questions of the Massilians and Pelagians put to him by Prosper and Hilary were resolved by Augustine in two books, namely On Predestination and On the Gift of Perseverance, written shortly before the day of his death. As to when Augustine died, Possidius relates it in the Life of Augustine, writing that in the year 430, on the fifth day before the Kalends of September, the holy doctor paid the debt of human life, at the time when the Vandals had already been besieging Hippo for the third month.
passages.notes: The fifth day before the Kalends of September is 28 August.

passages.original: Unum itaque dumataxat sancti Prosperi testimonium ex cap. 3 carminis de Ingratis depromptum adducunt, quo hocce opus su- I erstite Augustino conscriptum es"e sibi blaudiuutur. Canit itaque sanctus Prosper : An alium in finem posset procedere sanctum Concilium, cui dui Aurelius, ingeniumque Augustinus erat? quem Christi gratia cornu Uberiore rigans. uostro lumen dedit aevo Accensum vero de lumine; uam cibus illi, Et vita, et requies Deus est, omnisque voluplas; Unus arnor Christi est, unas Christi est bonor illi, Et dum nulla sibi tribuit bona, fit Deus illi Omnia, ei in sam io regnat sapieulia templo.
passages.english:
So they adduce only a single testimony of Saint Prosper, drawn from chapter 3 of the poem On the Ungrateful, by which they flatter themselves that this work was written while Augustine was still alive. Saint Prosper sings thus:
Could the holy council proceed to any other end,
whose leader was Aurelius, and whose genius was Augustine?
whom the grace of Christ, watering him from a richer horn,
gave as a light to our age,
kindled from the true light; for to him
God is food and life and rest and every pleasure;
his one love is Christ, his one honour is Christ,
and while he attributes no good things to himself, God becomes for him
all things, and wisdom reigns in a holy temple.
passages.notes: Many OCR errors in the verse corrected (e.g. 'dui' = dux, 'uam' = nam, 'sam io regnat sapieulia' = sancto regnat sapientia).
